title: On the select placeholder (label option)
body:
This is about two things:
1. it's not clear to me why the `select` has to have it's `required` attribute specified to denote the first option with an empty value as placeholder;
2. proposal to add placeholder attribute to the select element and deprecate the current placeholder spec.

#### 1. Current placeholder spec
From https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-elements.html#the-select-element:

> If a select element has a required attribute specified, does not have a multiple attribute specified, and has a display size of 1; and if the value of the first option element in the select element's list of options (if any) is the empty string, and that option element's parent node is the select element (and not an optgroup element), then that option is the select element's placeholder label option.

Why the `required` requirement?

And later:

> If a select element has a required attribute specified, does not have a multiple attribute specified, and has a display size of 1, then the select element **must** have a placeholder label option.

What's the reasoning behind this, why is it obligatory in this case? 


#### 2. Proposal: placeholder attribute
I'd much prefer an actual placeholder attribute just like the input and textarea elements have.
I figure the current placeholder spec is formed around according to how people already implemented this on their pages.
Though I think it'd be better to let the select have it's own placeholder attribute, and subsequently mark the current placeholder spec deprecated. Much cleaner, and consistent with the input & textarea elements.
